title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on potential IPO: 'We plan to be public'
html:
OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) CEO and co-founder Sam Altman said Wednesday that the ChatGPT maker is still planning to become a public company as rival Anthropic (ANT) nears the final stages of its Thursday listing.

"We plan to be public," Altman said at the New York Times DealBook Summit, adding that there are "many reasons why that's the right thing to do."

Altman said in September during an interview with Fortune that the company would not pursue an initial public offering in 2026 after reports that the major AI startup was going to try.

Anthropic, which was founded by former OpenAI employees and has made a more concerted effort to target business customers with its Claude AI tool suite, is expected to begin trading as a public company on Thursday in what could become the largest IPO ever.

Read more: Everything you need to know ahead of Anthropic's IPO

Altman acknowledged a growing "tension" for AI startups, saying that recent months have been a "really challenging period."

"There will be newly challenging periods ahead of us for a long time about the safety requirements in front of us," he warned.

Altman also responded to the fears surrounding the exponential growth of artificial intelligence with limited oversight. "If the world and the companies developing AI treated the next four years like they've treated the last four years, I think that would be very bad," he said.
At the same time, he noted that the "only way that we have known how to make this technology safe is to confront reality," meaning to test it in the real world.
Altman said OpenAI must strike a balance in its role in the AI safety conversation.

"If we talk too much about taking extra care for safety … people are going to accuse us of regulatory capture, or trying to slow down innovation," Altman said. If OpenAI focuses on innovation being "max pedal to the metal," he said, "People will say, 'Well, you know, please don't kill us all.'"
When asked about the departure of Nvidia (NVDA) founder and former CEO Jensen Huang, OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman said he has had personal discussions with Huang and his wife. "Jensen is singular," Brockman said.
"It's hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen," added Altman, who said he had also spoken with Huang. "Greg and I have, like, a little more empathy towards the situation than the average person."

In November 2023, OpenAI's board of directors ousted Altman, citing a lack of confidence in his ability to lead the AI startup. The same day, Brockman resigned in solidarity with Altman. However, five days later, OpenAI reinstated Altman after outcry from employees and investors.
summary: Sam Altman and Greg Brockman discussed OpenAI's potential IPO, advancing AI technology while ensuring safety, and Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia.
